question: According to the Census of India 2011, which state is the most densely populated?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Bihar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• According to the 2011 Census of India, **Bihar is the most densely populated state in the country**, with **1,102 people per square kilometer**.
 
• This is substantially higher than the **national average of 382 persons per sq. km**.
 
• Bihar is a landlocked state in the eastern part of India, and the third-largest state by population, after Uttar Pradesh and Maharashtra.
 
• Even though Uttar Pradesh is the most populous state in India, it does not have the highest population density due to its larger area.
 
• Similarly, Kerala and Haryana, although having high population densities, are not as densely populated as Bihar.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Census of India 2011 marked the **15th national census** of the country.
 
• It disclosed that India's total population was **1.21 billion**, an increase of 17.64% from the previous census in 2001.
 
• Notably, the sex ratio improved from 933 females per 1000 males in 2001 to 943 in 2011.
 
• However, there was a decline in Child Sex Ratio (0-6 years), from 927 in 2001 to 919 in 2011.
 
• The census revealed that there was an increase in literacy rate from 64.83% in 2001 to 74.04% in 2011.
 
• Despite housing less than 2.5% of the world population, India accounted for 17.5% of the global population.
 
• The population density increased to 382 persons per square kilometer.
 
• Another key finding was that the working-age population (15-59 years) increased from 58% in 2001 to 63% in 2011.
